questions.q: For the curtain-wall cross-section shown, which labeled part is the pressure plate?
questions.n: “C” is the pressure plate: the metal bar screwed into the mullion’s nose that clamps both glass edges against their gaskets. “B” is a gasket, “E” the insulating-glass spacer, and “F” the snap-on mullion cap that hides the plate.

questions.q: What term describes the structural member spanning above a window or door opening to carry the wall load over it?
questions.n: A lintel is the horizontal member that spans and carries load above a door or window opening.

questions.q: What is the brick position shown, a unit laid on its long edge with its end face exposed on the wall surface?
questions.n: A rowlock is laid on its long edge with the end showing, distinct from a shiner (laid on edge with the long face showing) or a stretcher (laid flat with the long face showing).

questions.q: What term describes waterproofing that is applied to the interior face of a basement or retaining wall, opposite the side where water pressure originates?
questions.n: “Negative side” refers to the face opposite the water source — the interior face of the wall — as distinct from the exterior (positive) face.

questions.q: What accessory is attached to a metal stud to prevent it from twisting during and after installation?
questions.n: Bridging channels are threaded through the punch-outs of a line of studs, bracing each stud against rotation.

questions.q: In the window-frame diagram shown, identify the part labeled “G”:
questions.n: “G” sits at the base of the assembly, just below the sill (“F”) — the trim piece occupying that position is the apron.

questions.q: What term describes a cutout made in a structural steel beam that removes material from the flange or web so that intersecting members can fit together?
questions.n: This is the same operation described earlier: coping trims the flange/web profile so a beam can fit around another member that crosses it.

questions.q: Which metal weathers into a distinctive green patina over time?
questions.n: Copper oxidizes on exposure to the atmosphere, forming verdigris (basic copper carbonate) — the green patina commonly seen on aged roofing and statues.

questions.q: Which metalworking process involves rapid cooling of heated metal?
questions.n: Quenching rapidly cools heated metal — typically in water or oil — to increase its hardness.

questions.q: Compute the combined R-value of a roof assembly consisting of 16-mm fiberboard, 1/8-inch glass sheet, and 3-inch rockwool, given resistivity (ρ) values of 2.4, 0.14, and 3.5 respectively:
questions.ref: R-value = thickness × resistivity, summed across layers
questions.n: Summing thickness × ρ for each layer (≈ 0.63 in × 2.4 for the fiberboard, 0.125 in × 0.14 for the glass, and 3 in × 3.5 for the rockwool) gives a total close to R-12.

questions.q: What masonry bond is shown, with headers and stretchers alternating within each course?
questions.n: In Flemish bond, headers and stretchers alternate within the same course, unlike English bond, which alternates whole courses.

questions.q: Which of the following products is NOT a water-based paint?
questions.n: Roofgard is a rubberized-asphalt, solvent/cutback-type roof coating, unlike Acrytex, Elasti-Kote, and Permacoat Latex, which are water-based.

questions.q: The steel section designation “W 8 X 18” indicates that:
o: the section's width is 8 in. and its depth is 18 in.
the section's width is 8 in. and its weight is 18 lb/ft.
the section's depth is 8 in. and its weight is 18 lb/ft.
the section's depth is 8 in. and its width is 18 in.
questions.n: AISC W-shape designations follow the pattern “W [nominal depth in inches] X [weight in lb/ft],” so “W8X18” denotes an 8-inch-deep section weighing 18 pounds per linear foot.

questions.q: What term describes a material assembly applied to a building as a non-load-bearing wall, or fastened to a wall surface purely for protection or ornament?
questions.n: Cladding is, by definition, a non-structural outer layer applied to a building envelope for protection or appearance.

questions.q: What term describes a formed, sawed, or tooled groove in concrete that creates a weakened plane to control where cracking occurs as the structure shrinks or moves?
questions.n: A contraction (control) joint is a tooled or sawed groove that induces cracking to occur along a predetermined, hidden line rather than randomly.

questions.q: What is the key distinction between wide-flange (W) steel shapes and standard S-shape I-beams?
o: Standard I-beams can serve as both beams and columns.
Standard I-beams may have equal or unequal leg dimensions.
Standard I-beams have flanges with sloped, tapered inner faces.
Standard I-beams have a constant thickness throughout their webs and flanges.
questions.ref: AISC Steel Construction Manual — shape definitions
questions.n: Wide-flange (W) shapes have essentially parallel-faced flanges of near-constant thickness, while S-shapes (standard I-beams) have tapered, sloped inner flange faces. That taper is the classic feature separating the two families.

questions.q: Hollow structural section (HSS) members are typically manufactured by:
o: bending and welding heated steel plates
bending and welding flat steel bars
questions.ref: Steel manufacturing (some cold-formed flat-strip processes also exist)
questions.n: HSS shapes are generally produced by rolling and welding heated flat steel into a closed tube profile.

questions.q: What is the minimum required Solar Reflectance Index (SRI) for metal roof surfaces under the Philippine Green Building Code?
questions.n: The Code requires metal roofing to either be finished white or carry a minimum SRI of 70, without exception.

questions.q: Regarding the relationship between water-cement ratio and concrete strength, which statement is correct?
o: It makes no difference — concrete strength depends solely on aggregate quality.
A higher proportion of cement relative to water produces stronger concrete.
A higher proportion of water relative to cement produces stronger concrete.
Equal proportions of water and cement produce the strongest concrete.
questions.n: A lower water-cement ratio — relatively more cement, less water — produces denser, stronger concrete. This relationship is known as Abrams' law.

questions.q: Based on typical-use guidance for gypsum panel products, which thickness is recommended for fire-resistant assemblies?
questions.n: 5/8-inch Type X board contains additives that improve fire performance and is the standard choice for fire-rated wall and ceiling assemblies.

questions.q: In steel framing, beams are sometimes cut and notched along the flange (and sometimes web) so that intersecting members can be welded together cleanly at odd angles. What is this fitting operation called?
questions.n: Coping removes part of a beam's flange, and sometimes its web, so the member can fit tightly around or into another beam that intersects it at an acute or obtuse angle.

questions.q: In the curtain-wall section, identify part “C”:
questions.n: “C” is the pressure plate: the bar screwed into the mullion that presses the glass against its gaskets. The spacer (E) sits between the two panes, and the mullion cap (F) snaps over the plate to cover it.

questions.q: Consider a prestressed concrete method where compression is applied on-site after the concrete has been poured and cured. The concrete is cast around a curved plastic, steel, or aluminum duct following the zone where tension would otherwise occur; once the concrete hardens, tendons are tensioned with hydraulic jacks bearing against the member itself, then wedged in place, the jacks removed, and the ducts filled with grout. This describes:
questions.n: The tendons pass through ducts embedded in the concrete and are stressed and anchored after curing; the ducts are later grouted, bonding the tendon to the surrounding concrete — the defining trait of a bonded post-tensioned system.

questions.q: Certain materials swell when exposed to heat — increasing in volume and decreasing in density — and are used as coatings or mastics that expand into a stable, insulating char during a fire. These materials are described as:
questions.n: Intumescent coatings expand on exposure to heat, forming a low-density insulating char that protects the substrate underneath — a key strategy in passive fire protection.

questions.q: Cementitious waterproofing performs best, in terms of long-term effectiveness, when applied on which side of a wall?
questions.n: Cementitious coatings work best on the positive (water-facing, exterior) side, sealing the surface before water can penetrate and build up pressure within the wall.

questions.q: Per the NSCP, all of the following are classified as deep foundation types EXCEPT:
questions.n: A mat (raft) foundation is a shallow foundation type. Caissons, drilled piers, and piles are the deep foundation types recognized by the Code.

questions.q: In the window-frame diagram, which labeled part is the sash?
questions.n: “E” is the sash: the frame of stiles and rails that holds the glass and sits inside the jambs. “C” and “D” are the head and side jambs, and “F” is the sill (stool).

questions.q: Based on typical-use guidance for gypsum panel products, which thickness is recommended for sound-attenuation partition systems?
questions.n: A lightweight 1/4-inch board is commonly used as a base layer in multilayer partitions built specifically to improve sound control.

questions.q: An asthmatic occupant who needs a non-allergenic insulation would be best served by which product?
questions.n: Cured closed-cell spray foam is inert and does not shed the airborne fibers or dust associated with fiberglass, rockwool, or cellulose, making it preferable for occupants sensitive to allergens.

questions.q: Which metalworking process involves gradual, controlled heating and cooling?
questions.n: Annealing uses slow, controlled heating and cooling to soften a metal and relieve internal stresses.

questions.q: Which type of glass is used for automotive windshields?
questions.n: Laminated glass — glass plies bonded around a PVB interlayer — stays intact on impact instead of shattering into loose fragments, which is why it's specified for windshields.

questions.q: What masonry bond is shown, with full courses of headers alternating with full courses of stretchers?
questions.n: English bond alternates a full course of headers with a full course of stretchers, rather than mixing them within a single course as Flemish bond does.

questions.q: Which of the following is a solvent-based paint product?
questions.n: Megacryl is a solvent-based acrylic lacquer finish; Acreex, Aqua Gloss-It, and Bio-Fresh are all water-based products.

questions.q: What accessory is attached to a roof purlin to keep it from twisting under load?
questions.n: Sag rods tie a line of purlins together across the roof slope, resisting the lateral component of load that would otherwise cause the purlins to twist or roll.

questions.q: Identify the concrete floor system illustrated:
questions.n: The illustration shows a flat soffit with thickened bands running over the column lines in both directions — the defining feature of a slab-with-slab-bands system, distinct from localized drop panels, ribbed slabs, or waffle slabs.

questions.q: Unlike barrier-type waterproofing products that only work at the concrete's surface, Xypex forms a crystalline structure deep within the concrete's own pores and capillaries to block water and aggressive chemicals. All of the following are valid ways to apply Xypex EXCEPT:
o: As an integral admixture, mixed directly into the fresh concrete
As an underlay, applied before the concrete is poured
As a dry-shake, applied to fresh concrete before finishing
questions.n: Because Xypex relies on crystalline growth within the concrete's own pore structure, it must contact the concrete directly — as a dry-shake, an integral admixture, or a surface coating — not as a separate layer laid down before the concrete is even poured.

questions.q: A greenish tint visible in ordinary float glass, especially along a thick edge, points to a high concentration of which impurity?
questions.ref: Soda-lime float glass composition — iron-oxide content
questions.n: Traces of iron oxide carried in by the silica sand tint soda-lime float glass green; the ferrous iron absorbs red light, which is why the cast is strongest looking through a thick edge. Manganese dioxide is added as a decolourizer, and cobalt oxide and selenium are deliberate colourants (blue, and pink to bronze).

questions.q: Which alloy is composed essentially of copper and zinc?
questions.n: Brass is, by definition, a copper-zinc alloy; bronze, by contrast, is a copper-tin alloy.

questions.q: Under the Philippine Green Building Code, roof insulation must provide an average thermal resistance (R-value) of at least:
questions.ref: Philippine Green Building Code, roof insulation provision
questions.n: The Code sets a minimum average roof R-value requirement of R-8.

questions.q: What term describes a resilient, brush-like or springy strip installed to reduce air infiltration, provide some soundproofing, and block dirt through the gap around a sash or door?
questions.n: Weatherstripping is specifically the resilient strip material used to seal gaps around movable sash and door edges.

questions.q: Which formwork-removal activity can only be carried out after a minimum of 14 days?
questions.ref: Standard formwork stripping-time tables (figures vary somewhat by span and code reference)
questions.n: Props supporting beams are typically left in place for a minimum of 14 days (longer for wider spans), whereas slab props can often be struck earlier depending on span — making beam props the item that specifically requires the 14-day minimum.

questions.q: Which glass thickness corresponds to a self-weight of roughly 30 kg per square meter?
questions.n: Glass weighs approximately 2.5 kg/m² per millimeter of thickness. At 12 mm, that works out to 12 × 2.5 = 30 kg/m², matching standard glass weight tables.

questions.q: A “jerkinhead” roof is best described as a:
questions.n: A jerkinhead roof is essentially a gable roof whose peak has been clipped back into a small hip, hence the description “hipped gable.”

questions.q: Consider a prestressed concrete method where each tendon is permanently free to move relative to the surrounding concrete. Individual strands are coated with a lithium-based grease and encased in an extruded plastic sheath, with force transferred to the concrete only through anchors at the perimeter. This describes:
questions.n: Because each grease-coated, plastic-sheathed tendon never bonds to the concrete around it, force transfers only through the end anchorages — the hallmark of an unbonded post-tensioned system.

questions.q: What is the most common interlayer material used to bond the glass plies in laminated glass?
questions.n: PVB is the standard interlayer used in laminated safety glass, such as windshields and hurricane glazing; EVA is a newer alternative used in some specialty applications.

questions.q: A control joint is sometimes needed in a masonry wall to accommodate shrinkage. In the assembly shown, which element functions as the bond breaker, keeping mortar from bridging across the joint?
questions.n: The asphalt-saturated paper strip prevents mortar from bonding across the joint, allowing the joint to function as a true control/expansion gap rather than a rigid bridge.

questions.q: What metal connector is used at glass corners to achieve a frameless, “all-glass” look on a curtain wall facade?
questions.n: Spider fittings are the multi-armed metal brackets bolted through the glass panels, used in point-supported structural glazing to eliminate visible framing.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the function of a plasticizer (water-reducing admixture) in concrete?
o: An admixture that increases slump without added water, or maintains slump with less water, through mechanisms other than air entrainment.
An admixture that decreases the heat of hydration of the cement and lengthens the setting time.
A concrete admixture that reduces the loss of fine material from concrete placed underwater.
An admixture that increases the rate of cement hydration, shortening setting time and speeding early strength gain.
questions.n: This is the standard ASTM C494 Type A/F definition of a water-reducer/plasticizer. The other options describe a retarder (a), an anti-washout agent (b), and an accelerator (c).

questions.q: Based on typical-use guidance for gypsum panel products, which thickness is recommended for curved wall or ceiling surfaces?
questions.n: The thin, flexible 1/4-inch board can bend to a tight radius without cracking, making it the standard choice for curved assemblies.

questions.q: Which material is the appropriate thinner/cleaner for latex-based paint?
questions.n: Latex paint is water-based, so plain water is used to thin and clean it up — solvent thinners like mineral spirits are reserved for oil-based paints.
